one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-29. No merger 8-K, 425 or joint release through 2026-11-01 (EDGAR). Events in the window: (1) a Lumentum definitive agreement 'as soon as mid next week' (CNBC 10-30) or a denial; at 'no big premium' my value effect is near zero, but the exchange ratio matters (struck on today's depressed MRVL price it is ~28% more shares than on 10-28's), so I expect a two-way move of roughly +/-10% on terms, slightly skewed down; a walk-away would likely lift the stock; (2) NVIDIA's Q3 FY27 results in the second half of November (AI-capex read-across); (3) Marvell's Q3 FY27 report is expected in early December, just outside the window. Short-horizon regularities: a mild reversal tendency after a -22% two-day drop offsets deal-dilution drift. I centre near spot (median ~$197.5) at about the usual monthly volatility (80%/3.5 = 23%; a little wider below for the deal-terms left tail). Unchanged from round 1: the supervisor's findings concern the 12-month value, not the one-month events.

fair_value.method: Driver build (AI capex x Marvell share of wallet, GM, opex; FY28 revenue $18.26B, FY29 $24.9B, horizon NTM non-GAAP EPS ~$8.87) valued at 28.8x NTM P/E (8-peer median 30.15x ex LITE, exit rule 30.03x, less 1.2 turns for post-horizon MRVL-specific risks) with weight 0.75, plus a normalised mid-cycle EPS $6.88 x 25x (0.25); less the Celestial AI earnout (-$0.8/share) and the Lumentum all-stock deal at expected value (p 0.42, -$0.57/share). Research target (12m) $238.10.

downside.story: 10th percentile (~$98): hyperscalers digest in CY2027-28 (AI capex 25% below the standing base, near the file's low case), Marvell content per capex dollar 8% lower (Trainium generation to Alchip, Microsoft dual-sources), custom mix takes GM 2pt lower, and the market pays ~18.8x for decelerating EPS; the Lumentum deal is signed at an ~8% premium and module makers move DSP orders (the dis-synergy sits at its high end).

base.story: Median: FY27 revenue $11.9B (Street $12.1B), FY28 $18.3B (+53%; mgmt ~$20B, Street $19.7B), FY29 $24.9B (MarketScreener $31.3B); non-GAAP op margin 39-42%; FY28 non-GAAP EPS ~$6.73 vs Street 7.33 (whisper ~7.45); 28.8x NTM at the horizon on ~$8.87; the Lumentum deal signs and closes with probability 0.42 at an ~8% premium and is roughly value-neutral at my LITE value (-$1.37/share if it happens, -$0.57 expected).

upside.story: 90th percentile (~$390): AI capex 25% above base (between base and the file's high case), share of wallet +8% (scale-up optics, Google TPU attach early), GM +1pt, multiple 33.8x; Lumentum either signs and is accepted as roughly neutral-to-accretive, or is dropped.

thesis_break_reason: At $125 MRVL would trade ~14x the build's horizon NTM EPS (~$8.87) and ~18.5x FY28 EPS ($6.73), below my normalised mid-cycle leg (~$171) by a quarter: only consistent with the downside drivers actually arriving (AI capex toward the standing view's low case, a confirmed loss of a major custom program such as Trainium/Maia) or a signed Lumentum deal with a large DSP-customer backlash. At that level something fundamental has broken rather than ordinary 80%-vol noise; my P10 (~$98) sits below it because the downside case is exactly that break.

sbc_treatment.note: Non-GAAP EBIT and EPS exclude SBC (peers' NTM P/E is on the same non-GAAP basis), so SBC is carried as dilution: shares +0.5%/yr net of ~$0.8B/yr buybacks. SBC is rising fast (TTM 828.9, Q2 FY27 326.2 = 12% of revenue incl. Celestial AI awards); at a lower share price the same dollars dilute more, a downside-case amplifier. Peers' NTM P/E (peers.md consensus) is on the same non-GAAP ex-SBC basis. Google warrant shares are added to the count as they vest (not as SBC).

reasoning: Round 2. Standalone first: the driver build (standing AI-capex base ex shells 1,155 / 1,751 / 2,155 $B x Marvell share 0.84% / 0.92% / 1.05%, Communications ~$2.15-2.25B, non-GAAP GM 58.4% -> 56.5%, opex 2.55 / 3.27 / 3.76 $B) gives revenue 11.9 / 18.3 / 24.9 $B and non-GAAP EPS 4.19 / 6.73 / 9.46 (Street 4.22 / 7.33; whisper ~4.26 / ~7.45; MarketScreener FY29 revenue 31.3B, my build 20% below; I stay below management's ~$20B FY28 because the share gain it needs is only half-evidenced: Benchmark's Trainium-loss call, dual-sourcing reports, custom-mix GM drag). Supervisor findings acted on: (a) the normalised leg normalised twice; it now uses the build's FY28-29 average revenue x a 34% mid-cycle margin ($6.88 x 25x = $171 vs $138); (b) LITE dropped from the peer median (30.15x on 8 peers), exit rule 30.03x, less 1.2 turns for MRVL-specific post-horizon risks priced from long_dated_risks = 28.8x; (c) the deal is now valued consistently: LITE on its own horizon NTM earnings (MarketScreener consensus, haircut 15% to match my MRVL haircut) at the exit-rule multiple = $114.5B, against 456.4M MRVL shares that are worth $108.9B at my standalone horizon value, plus a sized DSP dis-synergy from the Stifel switching risk (-$9.5B), +$3B synergies, -$1B costs: V -$1.27B, -$1.37/share if it happens. My round-1 -$12.3/share was mostly the asymmetry the supervisor found. (d) Probability re-derived 0.65 x 0.65 = 0.42, below the supervisor's 0.56: the Ahern-Sosyura large-firm caveat and the -22% reaction cut P(signed), and SAMR's record on US chip deals (Intel-Tower dead, Synopsys-Ansys held past its clock, Qualcomm-NXP) cuts P(close); I keep that view. One forward change of my own: FY29 share +5% (custom ~$9.5B) to credit part of the Investor Day custom raise. Result: research target (12m) $238.10 (standalone ~$238.7, deal -$0.57), downside case $98 (P10), upside case $390 (P90): a fatter left tail (ln down 0.89 vs up 0.49), since AI-capex digestion plus a de-rating compound. Skeptic evidence that still weighs: 21 insider sales and no buys in six months, rising SBC (12% of Q2 revenue), China 42% of revenue by ship-to, customer concentration.

downside.story: 10th percentile (~$98): hyperscalers digest in CY2027-28 (AI capex 25% below the standing base, near the file's low case), Marvell content per capex dollar 8% lower (Trainium generation to Alchip, Microsoft dual-sources), custom mix takes GM 2pt lower, and the market pays ~18.8x for decelerating EPS; the Lumentum deal is signed at an ~8% premium and module makers move DSP orders (the dis-synergy sits at its high end).

upside.story: 90th percentile (~$390): AI capex 25% above base (between base and the file's high case), share of wallet +8% (scale-up optics, Google TPU attach early), GM +1pt, multiple 33.8x; Lumentum either signs and is accepted as roughly neutral-to-accretive, or is dropped.

model_inputs.structure_note: Value is carried by the driver build (5 quarterly drivers: AI capex x Marvell share for Data center, Communications revenue, non-GAAP GM, non-GAAP opex) valued with a peer-anchored NTM P/E at the horizon (28.8x, weight 0.75) and a normalised mid-cycle P/E cross-check (0.25; stated EPS $6.88 from the build's FY28-29 average revenue at a 34% mid-cycle margin, not driver-linked). Adjustments: Celestial AI contingent consideration (p 1) and the Lumentum all-stock deal at expected value (p 0.42, V -1,268 $M). No DCF (policy), no SOTP: the two reported segments do not have separable peer multiples. METHOD FIT flag (thin XBRL TTM/market cap) does not weaken the P/E leg: revenue, operating income and shares are all tagged and the non-GAAP basis is reconciled in each release; the normalised leg is the non-multiple-driven check on cycle risk.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) dc_share path (0.84% -> 0.92% -> 1.05%) vs management's implied 1.03% in FY28: the mgmt FY28 path adds ~$20/share; (2) the -1.2 turns below the exit rule (30.03x -> 28.8x) for MRVL-specific post-horizon risks moves the target ~-3% (under the 5% card threshold); (3) Lumentum: p 0.42 and V -1,268 $M give -$0.57/share; V swings -$21 to +$17/share if it happens on the LITE haircut and the exchange-ratio reference price, so the deal is a variance item more than a value item in my set; the supervisor's p 0.56 would change the target by -$0.2; (4) FY2029 is a 53-week year (ends 2029-02-03), not annualised; (5) base-year AI capex (646) is a scaled secondary figure and only calibrates the base share. No financing event >=20% other than the deal itself (the deal is all stock; the adjustment carries its shares and LITE's earnings).
model_inputs.reverse_dcf_check: 28.8x NTM P/E at the horizon on ~$8.87 EPS (3.5% earnings yield) implies, at a ~10% cost of equity, roughly 15-18% EPS growth a year for about five years after FY2029 with ~40% non-GAAP operating margins held: plausible only if AI capex keeps growing past 2028 (standing view +23% in 2028) and Marvell keeps its custom programs, which is why the multiple carries 1.2 turns off the exit rule for those risks.
